$$\begin{array}{l}

$\left(a_{1}, b_{1}\right) R\left(a_{2}, b_{2}\right) \Leftrightarrow b_{1}=b_{2}$.
Statement-I: R is an equivalence relation.
Statement-II: For some $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) \in \mathrm{X}$, the set $\mathrm{S}=\{(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}) \in \mathrm{X}:(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}) \mathrm{R}(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b})\}$ represents a line parallel to $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}$.

(2) Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.

steps:
Statement - I :
Reflexive : $\left(\mathrm{a}_{1}, \mathrm{~b}_{1}\right) \mathrm{R}\left(\mathrm{a}_{1}, \mathrm{~b}_{1}\right) \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}_{1}=\mathrm{b}_{1} \quad$ True

\&\left(a_{2}, b_{2}\right) R\left(a_{3}, b_{3}\right) b_{2}=b_{3} \\
\Rightarrow\left(a_{1}, b_{1}\right) R\left(a_{3} . b_{3}\right) \Rightarrow \text { True }
\end{array}\right\} b_{1}=b_{3}$$

Hence Relation R is an equivence relation Statement-I is true.
